mainTopic: Liability of a renter who changes how a rented animal is used, hidden defects in a sale, and loading a rented donkey
overview: The משנה teaches that a renter who uses a rented cow differently from the agreement pays for damage only if his change made the damage more likely. The גמרא asks who pays for a broken plow when nothing was changed. The הלכה is that the one holding the plow pays, and on rocky ground both people pay. רבי יוחנן then teaches that a seller who hides a real defect among made-up ones has made a מקח טעות, and a ברייתא about a שפחה supports him. In the name of רבא, the גמרא adds that if every listed defect is real, the sale stands. A second משנה deals with loading a rented donkey with a different crop or with extra weight, and סומכוס gives the amount of extra load that makes the renter liable. אביי and רבא disagree on the wording of that משנה: does bulk count like weight? A proof for אביי from the משנה is rejected, and a new proof from a ברייתא begins that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Plowing on a different kind of land than agreed
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules on a broken plowshare when the renter plowed somewhere other than where he agreed: on easier land he is exempt, and on harder land he is liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone rents a cow to plow on the mountain but plows in the valley, and the plowshare breaks, he is exempt. If he rented it for the valley but plowed on the mountain, and the plowshare breaks, he is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה opens with a renter who used the cow and plow on a different type of ground than he agreed to.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Mountain ground is harder and rockier than valley ground. If he switched to easier ground, the change did not add any risk, so he is פטור. If he switched to harder ground, the change itself put the plow in danger, so he is חייב.

keyTerms.meaning: Plowshare, the cutting blade of the plow

steps.confusionAlert: Changing the agreement does not automatically make the renter liable. The משנה only makes him pay when the change made the damage more likely.

phrases.english: MISHNA: One who rents the cow
to plow on the mountain, but he plowed in the valley,
if the plowshare broke, he is exempt.
If he rented it to plow in the valley, but he plowed on the mountain,
if the plowshare broke, he is liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ הַשּׂוֹכֵר אֶת הַפָּרָה לַחֲרוֹשׁ בָּהָר
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A renter who switches to harder ground is liable for a broken plowshare. A renter who switches to easier ground is exempt.

steps.title: Threshing a different crop than agreed
steps.stepSummary: The משנה applies the same idea to threshing: switching from legumes to grain is exempt, and switching from grain to legumes is liable, because legumes are slippery.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he rented the cow to thresh legumes and it threshed grain, he is exempt. If he rented it to thresh grain and it threshed legumes, he is liable, because legumes are slippery.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a second example of the same rule, this time about threshing different crops.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Legumes like beans are slippery, so a cow treading on them can slip and get hurt. Switching from legumes to grain made the work safer, so he is exempt. Switching from grain to legumes added risk, so he is liable. The משנה states its reason openly: מפני שהקטנית מחלקת.

keyTerms.meaning: To thresh, having the cow trample the crop to separate the kernels
Legumes, such as beans and lentils

steps.whatToRemember: A renter who changes the agreement is responsible only when his change made the damage more likely.

phrases.english: If he rented it to thresh legumes, and it threshed grain, he is exempt;
phrases.notes: The משנה doesn't say what the damage is. It means the cow slipped and got hurt.

phrases.english: if he rented it to thresh grain, and it threshed legumes, he is liable,
because legumes are slippery.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second application of the same rule from step 1
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Switching to a riskier crop makes the renter liable. Switching to a safer crop leaves him exempt.

steps.title: Who pays when nobody changed the agreement?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks who pays for a broken plowshare when the renter plowed exactly as agreed.
steps.simpleTranslation: In a case where he did not change anything, who pays?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question the משנה left open. This sets up a disagreement between two אמוראים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only covered a renter who changed the deal. Now the גמרא wants to know what happens when the plow breaks during normal, agreed use. The question is which of the people working the plow should pay.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that explains the משנה

phrases.english: GEMARA: Where he did not deviate with it,
who pays?

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵיכָא דְּלָא שַׁנִּי בָּהּ, מַאן מְשַׁלֵּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the case the משנה did not address
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Who is responsible for a broken plowshare when there was no change from the agreement

steps.title: רב פפא: the one holding the goad pays
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says the person who drives the cow with the goad pays.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: The one who holds the goad pays.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא gives the first answer: the person steering the cow is responsible.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The goad is the stick used to direct the cow. In רב פפא's view, the person steering is to blame if the plow breaks, because he did not lead the cow along a straight, careful path.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who gives the first answer
Goad, a pointed stick for driving the cow

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
The one who holds the goad pays.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: דְּנָקֵיט פְּרָשָׁא מְשַׁלֵּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: First answer to the question in step 3
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The driver who holds the goad is responsible

steps.title: רב שישא: the one holding the plow pays
steps.stepSummary: רב שישא בריה דרב אידי disagrees and says the person holding the plow itself pays.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שישא, son of רב אידי, said: The one who holds the vessel pays.
steps.whatsHappening: A second אמורא gives a different answer: the person holding the plow is responsible.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the blame moves from the person steering the cow to the person guiding the plow into the ground. The plow is in his hands, so he is the one expected to keep it from breaking.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who disagrees with רב פפא
Vessel, here meaning the plow itself

phrases.aramaic: רַב שִׁישָׁא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִידִי אָמַר:
phrases.english: Rav Sheisha, son of Rav Idi, said:
The one who holds the vessel pays.
phrases.notes: "The vessel" here is the plow itself.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב שִׁישָׁא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִידִי אָמַר
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The one holding the plow is responsible

steps.title: The ruling, and the exception for rocky ground
steps.stepSummary: The הלכה follows רב שישא: the one holding the plow pays. In a place known to be rocky, both pay.
steps.simpleTranslation: The הלכה is that the one holding the plow pays. But if it is a place known for rocks, both of them pay.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא decides the disagreement in favor of רב שישא and adds one exception.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally the person holding the plow is the one responsible. On rocky ground, the plow can break from careless steering or from careless handling, so both people share the payment.
steps.whatToRemember: With no change from the agreement, the one holding the plow pays. On rocky ground, both the driver and the plow-holder pay.

phrases.english: And the halakha is: The one who holds the vessel pays.
And if it is a place that is known for rocks,
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets; the corrected wording is the word in square brackets. Both mean rocks.

phrases.english: both of them pay.

steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The plow-holder pays, and on rocky ground both people pay.

steps.title: Hiding a real defect among fake ones
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן teaches that a seller who lists several defects, only one of them real, has made a מקח טעות. A seller who says "this defect and other defects" has not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: If someone sells a cow and tells the buyer, "This cow gores, bites, kicks, and lies down," but it really has only one of those defects, which he slipped in among the others, the sale is a mistake. If he said "this defect and other defects," the sale is not a mistake.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new topic: a seller who mentions a real defect in a misleading way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The buyer can see that most of the listed defects are false, so he assumes the whole list is a joke and ignores the real defect too. That makes the sale a מקח טעות. If the seller clearly points out the real defect and only adds a vague "and others," the buyer was properly told, and the sale stands.

keyTerms.meaning: The אמורא who gives this teaching
He slipped it in, mixed it in
A mistaken sale, which can be canceled

steps.confusionAlert: The seller did mention the real defect. The problem is that he hid it among obviously false claims, so the buyer never really understood he was being warned.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: הַמּוֹכֵר פָּרָה לַחֲבֵירוֹ,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said: One who sells a cow to his fellow,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר לוֹ: פָּרָה זוֹ נַגְחָנִית הִיא,
phrases.english: and said to him: This cow is a gorer,

phrases.aramaic: נַשְׁכָנִית הִיא, בַּעֲטָנִית הִיא, רַבְצָנִית הִיא,
phrases.english: it is a biter, it is a kicker, it is a lier-down,
and it had only one defect
and he slipped it in among the defects,
this is a mistaken transaction.
If he said: This defect and another defect,
this is not a mistaken transaction.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: הַמּוֹכֵר פָּרָה לַחֲבֵירוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about defects in a sale
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A real defect hidden among false ones does not count as a proper warning, so the sale is a מקח טעות. Clearly naming the real defect plus a vague "and others" is a valid warning.
steps.whyThisMatters: It teaches that a warning only protects the seller when it was given in a way the buyer could actually take seriously.

steps.title: A ברייתא about a maidservant supports רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches the same rule about selling a שפחה with a list of defects, which supports רבי יוחנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is also taught in a ברייתא: If someone sells a maidservant and says, "She is foolish, epileptic, and deranged," but she has only one defect that he slipped in among the others, the sale is a mistake. If he said "this defect and other defects," it is not a mistake.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with the same rule, showing that רבי יוחנן's teaching matches an older source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case changes from a cow to a שפחה, but the logic is exactly the same. Hiding a real defect among false claims cancels the warning, while clearly naming it does not. The phrase תניא נמי הכי marks this as support, not a challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: It is also taught this way in a ברייתא

steps.whatToRemember: Whether the item is an animal or a servant, a defect is properly disclosed only when it is not buried among obviously false claims.

phrases.english: This is also taught in a baraita:
One who sells a maidservant to his fellow,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר לוֹ: שִׁפְחָה זוֹ שׁוֹטָה הִיא,
phrases.english: and said to him: This maidservant is an imbecile,
she is epileptic, she is crazy,
and she had only one defect
and he slipped it in among the defects,
this is a mistaken transaction.
If he said: This defect and another defect,
this is not a mistaken transaction.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי יוחנן's rule from step 7
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's rule about a defect hidden among false defects
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא with the identical rule about selling a שפחה

steps.title: What if every listed defect is real?
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרבא asks רב אשי about a case where all the defects the seller listed are really there.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא, son of רבא, asked רב אשי: if the cow or the maidservant really had all of these defects, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question builds on רבי יוחנן's rule. Here every defect the seller mentioned turns out to be real.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן taught that listing many defects when only one is real is a מקח טעות, because the buyer assumed the seller was exaggerating. The question now is whether the buyer can make the same claim when all of them are true: "I thought you were joking."

keyTerms.meaning: What is the law? (a standard way of asking a question)

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rav Acha, son of Rava, said to Rav Ashi:

phrases.aramaic: הָיוּ בָּהּ כׇּל הַמּוּמִין הַלָּלוּ, מַהוּ?
phrases.english: If she had all of these defects, what is the law?
phrases.notes: "She" can be the cow or the maidservant from the last two steps. Both were sold with a whole list of defects.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָיוּ בָּהּ כׇּל הַמּוּמִין הַלָּלוּ, מַהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends רבי יוחנן's rule to the case where all the listed defects are real.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the sale a מקח טעות when every listed defect is really present?

steps.title: רבא: the sale stands
steps.stepSummary: רב מרדכי reports in the name of רבא that if all the defects are real, it is not a מקח טעות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מרדכי said to רב אשי: this is what we say in רבא's name. If she had all these defects, it is not a mistaken sale.
steps.whatsHappening: The question gets its answer. The sale is valid, because the seller told the full truth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The seller was completely honest about every defect. If the buyer chose not to believe him, that is the buyer's problem, so he cannot cancel the sale.

keyTerms.meaning: A mistaken sale, which can be cancelled

steps.whatToRemember: Listing fake defects to hide a real one cancels the sale. Listing defects that are all true does not.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב מָרְדֳּכַי לְרַב אָשֵׁי,
phrases.english: Rav Mordechai said to Rav Ashi:
This is what we say in the name of Rava:
If she had all of these defects,
this is not a mistaken sale.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It is not a מקח טעות, because the seller told the truth.

steps.title: משנה: loading a rented donkey with a different crop
steps.stepSummary: The משנה teaches when a person who rents a donkey is liable for loading something other than what was agreed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Someone who rents a donkey to carry wheat but loads barley is liable. If he rented it for grain and loaded straw, he is liable, because bulk is as hard on the animal as weight. If he rented it to carry a לתך of wheat and loaded a לתך of barley, he is exempt. If he adds to the load, he is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens a new topic: the renter's liability for how he loads a rented animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first two cases the weight stays the same, but the lighter crop takes up more space. That extra bulk strains the animal, so he is liable. In the לתך case the volume stays the same and the weight is lighter, so he is exempt.

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
One who rents a donkey
to carry wheat on it,
and he carried barley on it, is liable.
phrases.notes: This means the same weight of barley. Barley is lighter, so the same weight takes up more space.

phrases.english: If he rented it for grain and carried straw on it, he is liable,
because bulk is as hard as the load.
If he rented it to carry a לתך of wheat
and carried a לתך of barley, he is exempt.
And if he adds to its load, he is liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַשּׂוֹכֵר אֶת הַחֲמוֹר לְהָבִיא עָלֶיהָ חִטִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה with a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Same weight with more bulk makes him liable. Same volume with less weight leaves him exempt. Adding to the load makes him liable.

steps.title: משנה: how much extra makes him liable
steps.stepSummary: סומכוס in the name of רבי מאיר gives the amount of added load that makes the renter liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: How much must he add to the load to be liable? סומכוס says in the name of רבי מאיר: a סאה for a camel, three קבין for a donkey.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה defines how much "adding to the load" has to be.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A tiny addition does not count. The amount depends on the animal's size: a larger amount for a camel, a smaller one for a donkey.

keyTerms.meaning: A measure equal to six קבין
Plural of קַב, a smaller measure

phrases.aramaic: וְכַמָּה יוֹסִיף עַל מַשָּׂאוֹ וִיהֵא חַיָּיב?
phrases.english: And how much must he add to its load to be liable?
Sumchos says in the name of Rabbi Meir:
A סאה for a camel, three קבין for a donkey.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכַמָּה יוֹסִיף עַל מַשָּׂאוֹ וִיהֵא חַיָּיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the amount of the "addition" mentioned in step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A סאה extra for a camel and three קבין extra for a donkey make him liable.

steps.title: אביי and רבא argue over the משנה's wording
steps.stepSummary: אביי reads the משנה as "קשה כמשאוי" and רבא reads it as "קשה למשאוי."
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: אביי said we learned "bulk is hard LIKE the load." רבא said we learned "bulk is hard FOR the load."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with a disagreement about one letter in the משנה. The next step will explain what each reading means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two readings differ only in the letter כ ("like") versus ל ("for"). That small change will lead to a real difference in when the renter is liable.

keyTerms.meaning: It was stated (introduces a disagreement between אמוראים)

steps.confusionAlert: Read the letters carefully. אביי's reading has כְּ (like), and רבא's reading has לְ (for). The whole argument depends on that one letter.

phrases.english: GEMARA: It was stated:
Abaye said: we learned "hard like the load."
Rava said: we learned "hard for the load."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Analyzes the wording of the משנה in step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There are two readings of the משנה: כְּמַשּׂאוֹי and לְמַשּׂאוֹי.

steps.title: What each reading means in practice
steps.stepSummary: אביי says bulk counts just like weight. רבא says the case is one of equal weight, where the extra bulk is itself the addition.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said we learned "like the load": bulk is like weight, so if he adds three קבין, he is liable. רבא said we learned "for the load": weight is like weight, and the extra bulk counts as the addition.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats each reading and explains the rule that follows from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For אביי, bulk is treated exactly like weight. So when he loads the same volume and adds three קבין more, he is liable. For רבא, the משנה's case is one where the weights are equal, and the extra bulk is what counts as the addition. So when the volume is the same, adding three קבין is not enough to make him liable.

phrases.english: Abaye said: we learned "hard like the load,"
meaning bulk is like weight,
and if he adds three קבין, he is liable.
Rava said: we learned "hard for the load,"
meaning when weight is like weight,
the bulk counts as the addition.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the practical result of each reading in step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אביי: an addition of three קבין makes him liable. רבא: when the weights are equal, the extra bulk is the addition, and three קבין with equal volume is not enough.

steps.title: Trying to prove אביי from the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that "if he added to the load" in the משנה means three קבין, which would support אביי.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned: if he rented it to carry a לתך of wheat and carried a לתך of barley, he is exempt, and if he added to the load, he is liable. Doesn't that mean three קבין?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the משנה itself to try to prove אביי's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Right after the case of equal volume, the משנה says that adding makes him liable. If that addition is three קבין, then three קבין on top of equal volume makes him liable, which is exactly אביי's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Isn't it that...? (introduces a suggested proof)

phrases.english: We learned: if he rented it to carry a לתך of wheat
and carried a לתך of barley, he is exempt.
And if he added to its load, he is liable.
Isn't it that he added three קבין?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to decide the argument of step 14 in favor of אביי.
steps.raayaObject: אביי's view that three קבין on top of equal volume makes him liable
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's words "ואם הוסיף על משאו חייב"

steps.title: No, the addition is a סאה
steps.stepSummary: The proof is pushed off: the משנה's addition could be a full סאה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof for אביי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the extra amount was a whole סאה, everyone agrees he is liable, and רבא can agree too. So the משנה no longer proves anything about three קבין.

phrases.english: No, a סאה.

steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the reading that the addition is three קבין
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה's addition could be a full סאה, which fits רבא as well.

steps.title: But the משנה itself says three קבין for a donkey
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the push-off: the same משנה explicitly says three קבין for a donkey.
steps.simpleTranslation: But on this very case the משנה teaches: how much must he add to be liable? Sumchos says in the name of רבי מאיר: a סאה for a camel, three קבין for a donkey!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer "a סאה" by quoting the next line of the same משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our case is about a donkey, and the משנה says plainly that for a donkey the amount is three קבין. So reading the addition as a סאה seems to go against the משנה, and the proof for אביי seems to come back.

keyTerms.meaning: It teaches about this very case

phrases.english: But it teaches on this very case:

phrases.aramaic: וְכַמָּה יוֹסִיף עַל מַשָּׂאוֹ וִיהֵא חַיָּיב?
phrases.english: "How much must he add to its load to be liable?"
"Sumchos says in the name of Rabbi Meir:"
"A סאה for a camel, three קבין for a donkey!"

steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the משנה's addition is a סאה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same משנה says that for a donkey the amount is three קבין, not a סאה.

steps.title: The three קבין rule is only for the same kind of grain
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the last part of the משנה is a separate case. The renter did not switch grains, and for that case סומכוס in the name of רבי מאיר gives a סאה for a camel and three קבין for a donkey.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what the משנה means: when the renter did not change anything (he agreed on wheat and brought wheat, or agreed on barley and brought barley), how much must he add to the load to become liable? סומכוס says in the name of רבי מאיר: a סאה for a camel, three קבין for a donkey.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 17 by reading the 'three קבין' clause as its own separate case. In that case the renter carried the same type of grain he agreed to.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 17 argued that the משנה itself says the addition is three קבין, so it cannot be a סאה. The answer is that three קבין is the amount only when the grain type stayed the same. The earlier phrase 'if he added to the load' can still be about a different, larger amount, so the push-off from step 16 survives and the proof for אביי still does not work.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 17 and keeps the push-off of step 16 standing.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading the משנה: the last clause is split off as a separate case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The 'three קבין' clause explains the earlier 'if he added to the load,' so that addition must be three קבין.
steps.terutzMaskana: The 'three קבין' clause is only about a renter who kept the same grain. The earlier addition may still be a סאה, so the משנה does not prove אביי's view.
steps.whatToRemember: The three קבין / one סאה amounts apply when the renter carried the same kind of grain he agreed to. The attempted proof for אביי from the משנה falls away.

steps.title: A new proof begins from a case of a לתך of wheat
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens a new attempted proof from a ברייתא. Someone hired an animal to carry a לתך of wheat and then brought something else. The quote continues beyond this section.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: if he hired it to bring a לתך of wheat, and he brought…
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new proof about bulk versus weight, the argument between אביי and רבא. Only the opening words of the ברייתא appear here, and the rest continues next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'תא שמע' tells us a source is being brought to test one of the views. The case starts with an agreed load of a לתך of wheat. What the renter actually brought, and what we learn from it, comes in the next part.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the משנה-based proof fell away in step 18, the גמרא turns to a ברייתא to test אביי and רבא.
steps.raayaObject: The argument between אביי and רבא over whether extra bulk counts like extra weight.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about hiring an animal to carry a לתך of wheat (the quote is not yet complete).
